items.item: Each category in the tree shows a product count, the page states whether counts include subcategories, and in the sample data every parent's total equals its own products plus the totals of its children
items.evidence: Tree rows show counts via computeCount(node) (e.g. Electronics=2,418, Audio=612) and the math is internally consistent (Audio 612 = Headphones 184 + Speakers 428), but nowhere does the UI state whether displayed counts include subcategory products — no label like 'includes subcategories' appears near the tree count or the detail panel's 'Products in this category' stat (page.html lines 290-307, 392-394).

items.item: The tree exposes its structure to screen readers (role="tree" and "treeitem", or nested lists) with aria-expanded on parent nodes and the selected node marked, and nodes can be expanded, collapsed and selected from the keyboard
items.evidence: The tree is built entirely from <div>/<button> elements in renderNode() (page.html lines 285-314) with no role="tree"/"treeitem" and no <ul>/<li> nesting, no aria-expanded on the toggle buttons, and no aria-selected/aria-current on the selected row (selection is shown only via a CSS class 'bg-ink/[0.07] border-l-2 border-ink'). A grep of the whole file for role=, aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-current and tabindex returns zero matches.

items.item: Searching by name keeps the ancestors of each matching category visible and expanded so its place in the hierarchy is clear, and a search with no matches says so
items.evidence: renderNode() returns '' for a node unless nodeMatchesOrDescendant(node, query) is true, and forces isOpen = true while searching (page.html lines 286-291), so ancestors of a match stay visible/expanded. renderTree() shows 'No categories match "<query>". Try a different search term.' when nothing matches (line 325).

items.item: The detail panel shows the selected category's full path (such as "Home › Kitchen › Cookware"), name, URL slug, parent, visibility status, product count with a link to those products, and the last modified date and user
items.evidence: Breadcrumb path, name (h1), slug ('/electronics/audio/headphones'), and a status <select> are rendered (page.html lines 378-390), but the product count ('Products in this category', line 393) is plain text with no link/anchor to a filtered product list, and there is no 'last modified' date or user field anywhere in renderDetail().

items.item: Hidden or inactive categories are marked in the tree with a text label or icon (such as "Hidden"), not only by greying out
items.evidence: Status is shown only as a 2px coloured square via chipClass(node.status) (teal/amber/slate) with an invisible 'title' tooltip attribute (page.html line 305); e.g. draft nodes 'Smart Home' and 'Camping' show only an amber dot in the screenshot with no on-screen text like 'Draft'/'Hidden' next to the name in the tree.

items.item: Deleting a category that still has products or subcategories is blocked or requires choosing where to move them, and the confirmation names the category and the counts affected
items.evidence: deleteNode() (page.html lines 267-274) always deletes the node and its subtree with no blocking logic. The confirmation only reads 'Delete "<name>" and its subcategories?' (line 371) — it names the category but never states product or subcategory counts, and offers no option to reassign/move children.

items.item: A category can be given a new parent without drag-and-drop (a parent picker or "Move to…" action), and the picker excludes the category itself and its own descendants
items.evidence: No move/reparent feature exists anywhere in the script — there is no 'Move to…' control, parent picker, or any code referencing reassigning node.parent after creation.

items.item: Selecting another category while the detail form has unsaved edits asks to save or discard first
items.evidence: handleClick()'s data-select branch unconditionally does 'selectedId = ...; editingDescription = false; ... render();' (page.html line 456) with no check of the editingDescription state or any confirm dialog, so switching selection while editing the description silently discards the edit.

items.item: With nothing selected the detail panel shows a prompt instead of blank fields, a catalogue with no categories offers to create the first one, and the tree has loading and load-error-with-retry states
items.evidence: renderDetail() falls back to 'const node = findById(selectedId) || CATALOG[0] || null' so a category is always auto-selected and the empty-catalogue message 'No categories yet. Create one to get started.' (line 337) only fires if CATALOG itself is empty. There is no loading state and no load-error/retry UI anywhere — CATALOG is a hard-coded in-page array with no async fetch at all.

notes: This is a static mock (hard-coded CATALOG array, no fetch/loading/error states). Automated audit score is 96/100 with only a minor type-scale warning (8 font sizes). No classic AI-dashboard template tells were found: no greeting header, KPI icon tiles, delta pills, avatars, gradients, glass/blur, tracked-uppercase labels, emoji icons, rainbow status pills, sidebar promo card, decorative charts, card-in-card nesting, hover-lift effects, oversized radii (radii metric is a flat 2px), or navy-sidebar/indigo-accent styling — the visual design is a restrained, muted editorial palette (ink/paper/teal/amber/rust). Functional gaps are concentrated in accessibility (no tree/treeitem roles, no aria-expanded/aria-selected) and in workflow safety (delete, reparent, unsaved-edit guard, loading/error states) rather than in visual template tells.
